symptom: `boundary event interrupting timer addDays([%CurrentDateTime%], 3) caption 'Escalate' { … }` failed with "mismatched input 'caption' expecting ';'" and a misleading hint that 'Caption' is a keyword to quote; every timer boundary event mxcli wrote had an empty Caption in Studio Pro, and the rewrite guard of #1713 had to refuse a stored one
cause: workflowBoundaryEventClause gave a timer no caption slot, although Workflows$InterruptingTimerBoundaryEvent / NonInterruptingTimerBoundaryEvent have Caption and every writer already emitted the key (always ""); the reader read it and describe never printed it
insight: A delay is optional and is an expression, so a new keyword after it must be excluded from the delay's first token too: `interrupting timer caption 'X'` would otherwise parse `caption` as the delay expression (the same reason `non` already was, ako/mxcli#753) — add CAPTION and its alias COMMENT to the workflowTimerDelay predicate and test the no-delay form. Reuse workflowCaption rather than a bare string: notification events already use the bare string as caption, so a timer's string would read as its delay. Changing the WorkflowMutator interface means three implementations (wfmutator, mcp, mock) and every test call site; a small arg-aware script beats sed for the call sites because delays contain commas
fix: Accept workflowCaption after a timer's delay (create and alter insert), build it into BoundaryEvent.Caption, pass it through InsertBoundaryEvent to the writers, print `caption '…'` in describe, and drop the timer-caption reason from the #1713 refusal
